abstract: Intratumor heterogeneity is a hallmark of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that contributes to therapy resistance and poor clinical outcomes. Using patient-derived HCC organoids (HCCOs), we examine whether this diversity can be regenerated from single tumor cells. Across nine HCCO lines, a large proportion of individual cells give rise to new organoids, indicating that clonogenic capacity is broadly distributed rather than confined to a rare subset. Single-cell-derived HCCOs (scd-HCCOs) regenerate heterogeneous marker expression and display variable proliferation and drug responses. Single-cell RNA sequencing shows that parental and clonal organoids share a common repertoire of transcriptional states, with individual scd-HCCOs differing mainly in the relative abundance of these states. Serial single-cell cloning shows that functional traits diversify again in each generation, and whole-exome sequencing reveals few new point mutations but substantial copy-number variation. Single HCC cells therefore regenerate the marker, transcriptional, and functional diversity of the organoids they derive from.
